title: Every omega-tree with finite levels contains a leafless balanced subtree with omega levels
author: Supakun Panasawatwong; J. K. Truss
difficulty_reason: The lemma produces, inside any tree with omega finite levels, a subtree that is balanced, has no leaves and still has omega levels (statement lines 491-492). The proof schedules prunings according to a sequence in which every natural number occurs infinitely often, at each stage keeping only the nodes of the scheduled level that have infinitely many points above them and, among those, the minimum degree, and then takes the intersection of the resulting decreasing sequence of subtrees (proof lines 494-506). The two steps that carry the content are the choice of the minimum-degree pruning, which is what produces equal degrees on each level, and the argument that the levels of the intersection are eventually constant, which uses that each level is scheduled infinitely often and the levels are finite (proof lines 500-511). Leaflessness then follows because nodes survive with successors at every stage. H2.
